guideposts.label: Cycling history in Vall d’Alba
guideposts.detail: Vall d’Alba is a La Vuelta stage town for the first time*. Vall d’Alba was the setting of the time trials at the 2018 Spanish national championships. Jonathan Castroviejo won the men’s elite title and Mavi Garcia the women’s elite title. *The full list of new stage towns in this edition: Monaco (stage 1), Manosque (2), Font-Romeu (stage 3), Falset (5), Roquetes (5), Vall d’Alba (7), Puçol (8), Xer

guideposts.label: Pogacar made it 3 already at La Vuelta 26, and 38 in total in Grand Tours
guideposts.detail: Yesterday, Tadej Pogacar became the first rider with three stage wins in the first six days of La Vuelta since Oscar Freire in 2007. With a 38th Grand Tour stage win (26 in the Tour, 6 in La Vuelta, 6 in the Giro), he passed Rik Van Looy (37) as the 9th all time best scorer. Delio Rodriguez and Learco Guerra are tied at 7th place with 39 wins each. The former took all these victories in La Vuelta:

guideposts.label: Mas joined the list of runner-ups to Pogacar
guideposts.detail: Although Enrica Mas was 2nd to Tadej Pogacar at Il Lombardia 2022 (a week after beating him at the Giro dell’Emilia) and in stages 2 and 4 of the Vuelta a Andalucia 2023, yesterday was the first time they finished 1st and 2nd in a Grand Tour stage. It makes Mas the 20th rider to finish second to Pogacar in a Grand Tour stage. Ethan Hayter and Jarno Widar also joined that list during La Vuelta 26:

guideposts.label: Team standings
guideposts.detail: With Felix Gall (6th), Matthew Riccitello (23rd) and Gregor Mühlberger (25th), Decathlon CMA CGM had the best collective performance yesterday and took the lead of the team standings ahead of UAE Emirates XRG (+4’22’’) and Netcompany Ineos (+16’01’’).

guideposts.label: Stage 7 is ON!
guideposts.detail: Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) immediately attacks.

guideposts.label: 3 attackers: Van Aert, Vader, Leknessund
guideposts.detail: Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) accelerated as soon as the flag dropped. Milan Vader (Bahrain Victorious) and Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility) are with them. The peloton trail by 27'' at km 3.

guideposts.label: 4 chasers
guideposts.detail: Paul Ourselin (Cofidis), Hannes Wilksch (Tudor), Timo Roosen (Picnic PostNL) and Ivan Cobo (Kern Pharma) try to join the lead trio.

guideposts.label: The gap significantly increases
guideposts.detail: The lead trio are already at km 9. The four chasers trail by 1'. New counter-attackers set off from the b unch, already two minutes behind the leaders.

guideposts.label: Wout van Aert, Milan Vader and Andreas Leknessund
The chasers are caught by the bunch at km 16
guideposts.detail: Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike), Milan Vader (Bahrain Victorious) and Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility) are 1'20'' ahead.

guideposts.label: 2 leaders: Van Aert and Leknessund
guideposts.detail: Vader is dropped from the breakaway at km 19.

guideposts.label: 20 kilometres of battle
guideposts.detail: Many riders try to counter-attack a minute behind the lead duo. We've just seen Jesus Herrada (Burgos Burpellet BH) try to get away. Today is quite a special day for the Spaniard...

guideposts.label: Herrada on the move on "home roads"?
guideposts.detail: Many Spanish riders (as well as Colombia’s Sergio Higuita) are used to training in the area, part of the Sierra de Gudar, next to the Sierra de Javalambre. It’s the case of Jesus Herrada (Burgos Burpellet BH), who is set to retire at the end of La Vuelta 26. Today’s course echoes the first of his three La Vuelta victories, in 2019: the stage started in Mora de Rubielos (km 122 on today’s course) a

guideposts.label: 3 new chasers: Lutsenko, Bisiaux, Zana
guideposts.detail: Alexey Lutsenko (NSN) and Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM) already attacked together yesterday. They are joined by Italy's Filippo Zana (Soudal Quick-Step). More attackers try to ge in the mix.

guideposts.label: Another chase duo
guideposts.detail: Van Aert and Leknessund have passed km 30. +30'' Bisiaux, Lutsenko, Zana +40'' Martin-Guyonnet, Garcia Pierna +50'' Peloton, with more attacks

guideposts.label: A strong chase group on the move
guideposts.detail: Tobias Johannessen (Uno-X Mobility) is up there, as well as Larry Warbasse (Tudor), Ben Turner (Netcompany Ineos), Pello Bilbao (Bahrain Victorious), Ivan Sosa (Kern Pharma)...

guideposts.label: Pedersen joins the chase group
guideposts.detail: After 40 kilometres, they are 40 seconds behind the lead duo.

guideposts.label: Paret-Peintre joins the chase group
guideposts.detail: With under 5 kilometres to the summit, they are 35'' behind the leaders.

guideposts.label: 3 more attackers set off from the bunch
guideposts.detail: Sergio Samitier (Cofidis), Juan Felipe Rodríguez (EF Education-EasyPost) and Mats Wenzel (Equipo Kern Pharma) are 2 minutes behind the lead duo and 15 seconds ahead ot he peloton.

guideposts.label: 5 leaders into the last kilometre of ascent
guideposts.detail: Eddie Dunbar (Pinarello Q36.5), Alexey Lutsenko (NSN) and Tobias Johannessen (Uno-X Mobility) join Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) and Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility) at the front. The first chasers trial by 40 seconds, and the peloton by 2'30''.

guideposts.label: Results at Puerto El Remolcador (cat. 2, km 55.2)
guideposts.detail: 1. Leknessund, 5 pts 2. Lutsenko, 3 pts 3. Johannessen, 1 pt

guideposts.label: The gaps at the summit
guideposts.detail: +35'' 19-man chase group +50'' Samitier, JF Rodriguez, Wenzel +2'25'' Peloton

guideposts.label: Samitier, Rodriguez and Wenzel join the chase group
guideposts.detail: That makes 22 riders 50 seconds behind the five leaders, who are at the bottom of the second climb of the day, the cat. 3 Alto de Zucaina.

guideposts.label: Halfway through the stage
guideposts.detail: The five leaders enter the second half of the stage (75 km to go) with a gap of 1'20'' to the chase group. The peloton trail by 3'40''.

guideposts.label: Warbasse (kind of) knows today's challenges
guideposts.detail: Larry Warbasse (Tudor) is one of five La Vuelta 26 riders who climbed Aramon Valdelinares in 2014. Now he's in the breakaway alongside Marco Brenner. Just this morning, on the bus right here, I was checking to see the last time they did it in the Vuelta, and it was 2014, and that was my first Vuelta", Warbasse said at the start. "I was like ‘oh wow, I guess I’ve done the climb before’. I went and

guideposts.label: The average speed after 2 hours: 42.6 km/h
guideposts.detail: The five leaders are about to enter the final 60 kilometres. +1'40'' Chase group +3'55'' Peloton

guideposts.label: Bad cooperation in the chase group
guideposts.detail: Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM) tried to split the chase group but he's reeled in. They are 1'45'' behind the five leaders.

guideposts.label: The 3rd La Vuelta finish at Aramon Valdelinares
guideposts.detail: Aramon Valdelinares has hosted two La Vuelta stage finishes. In 2005, Roberto Heras took the stage and the overall lead. In 2014, two Colombians shared the glory: Winner Anacona won the stage ahead of Alexey Lutsenko, and Nairo Quintana took La Roja for the first time in his career. guideposts.label: 5 La Vuelta 26 riders were already at Aramon Valdelinares in 2014
guideposts.detail: - Alexey Lutsenko, 2nd of the stage - Pello Bilbao, 5th - Mikel Landa, 49th - Larry Warbasse, 93rd - George Bennett, 101st For both Lutsenko and Bilbao, it was their first top 10 result in a Grand Tour. Bilbao and Warbasse were doing their first Grand Tour.

guideposts.label: 35 kilometres to go
guideposts.detail: The five leaders are headed for the intermediate sprint (26.5 km to go). The gap to the chasers is stable: 1'15''. The gap to the bunch is up to 5'50''.

guideposts.label: Wout van Aert (Visma | Lease a Bike)
Bisiaux reacts
guideposts.detail: Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM) accelerates. The strongest climbers from the chase group follow the French youngster, starting with his compatriot Valentin Paret-Peintre (Soudal Quick-Step).

guideposts.label: 15 kilometres to go
guideposts.detail: Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike), Eddie Dunbar (Pinarello Q36.5), Tobias Johannessen, Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility) and Alexey Lutsenko (NSN) are inside the last 2 kilometres of the penultimate climb.

guideposts.label: Results at Puerto de San Rafael (cat. 2, km 135.3)
guideposts.detail: 1. Van Aert, 5 pts 2. Lutsenko, 3 pts 3. Leknessund, 1 pt

guideposts.label: Gall attacks
guideposts.detail: He is followed by Pogacar and Mas. Roglic and Onley are a few metres behind.

guideposts.label: Andreas Leknessund wins stage 7 of La Vuelta 2026
guideposts.detail: His team's first success in the Spanish Grand Tour... And it will be a 1-2 with Johannessen!

guideposts.label: Top 5
guideposts.detail: 1. Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility) 2. Tobias Johannessen (Uno-X Mobility), +34'' 3. Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike), +47'' 4. Jakob Omrzel (Bahrain Victorious), +58'' 5. Juan Felipe Rodriguez (EF Education-EasyPost), +1'13''
